faq.q: What is the origin of Abaid?
faq.a: Abaid is associated with Arabic. Diminutive of عبد (ʿabd), hence 'little servant, devoted servant'. The source record's gloss 'Servant of Allah' is imprecise.
Yes — the underlying form عبيد is Arabic.
Abaid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abaid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. root ع ب د occurs in the Qur'an; عبيد is a normal Arabic diminutive, not a Qur'anic proper name

faq.a: Romanization variants include Abaid, abaid. Script forms are عبيد, عبید, उबैद.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
